name: Jervis Bay Wild
summary: Whale and dolphin cruises, sightseeing passages, sunset cruises and in-water swims from the public wharf at Huskisson on Jervis Bay, New South Wales. The operator also runs guided kayaking, kayak, SUP and bike hire, and private charters on a sailing catamaran. Whale cruises run from mid-May to mid-November and dolphin cruises run all year.
standouts: Holds Advanced Eco-certification, as stated on the About page
More than 15 years operating in Jervis Bay Marine Park, 365 days a year including public holidays
States it holds the permit for in-water humpback whale experiences in Jervis Bay (operator blog, September 2026)

contact.address: Booking office: 58 Owen Street, Huskisson NSW. Cruises leave from the public wharf near Fishermens Wharf Restaurant; the site's footer address is 15 Field Street, Huskisson NSW 2540

trips.title: Whale Cruise
trips.summary: A 2 to 3 hour cruise to watch humpback whales migrating past Jervis Bay, from mid-May to mid-November. The whales head north from May to August, and from September to November mothers and calves rest in the sheltered bay. It runs seven days a week, including public holidays.
highlights: Humpback whales on the northern migration, May to August
Mothers and calves resting in the bay, September to November
Departs 10am and 1pm, seven days including public holidays
Check in 30 minutes before departure at the vessel
trips.departsFrom: Public wharf, Huskisson, near Fishermens Wharf Restaurant
trips.requirements: Dogs cannot join the whale cruise.
trips.checkNotes: No prices on the site: fares appear only inside the FareHarbor booking widget, which was not opened. Season is stated as mid-May to mid-November on the trip page and as May to November on cards and the FAQ; used the trip page. The page says cruise times may change with the tide. Dog rule is from the FAQ. The page's statement that humpbacks are what guests will see was not repeated.

trips.title: Dolphin Cruise
trips.summary: A 1.5 hour cruise from Huskisson to see the resident bottlenose dolphins of Jervis Bay Marine Park, all year round. In summer, guests can add a boom net, which is towed behind the boat through the water. It runs seven days a week, including public holidays, and times change with the tide.
highlights: Resident bottlenose dolphins that live in the bay all year
Boom net add-on in summer, added when booking on departures that run it
Check in 30 minutes before departure at the vessel
Dogs welcome on the larger boats
trips.departsFrom: Public wharf, Huskisson, near Fishermens Wharf Restaurant
bring: For boom netting: towel and swimmers
trips.requirements: Boom net: children under 2 cannot board the net. Ages 2 to 14 must be accompanied by an adult, and at the crew's request children sit on a parent's lap. All swimming abilities can join. Dogs are welcome on the larger boats but not the smaller boats, so contact the office before booking.
trips.checkNotes: No prices on the site: fares appear only inside the FareHarbor booking widget, which was not opened. The booking box lists Boom Netting as a second line, but both buttons open the same FareHarbor item, and the page says it is not a separate booking. Departure times are not stated (they vary with the tide). Dolphin numbers conflict: the trip page says more than 100 resident dolphins, the FAQ says between 80 and 90, so no count is given here. Dog and boom net rules are from the FAQ.

highlights: Three packages: own gear, gear supplied, or stay on board
The swim is never guaranteed
Crew look for whales along the South Coast and enter the water only when behaviour and conditions allow
Guests may also see dolphins, seals and other marine life

trips.title: Jervis Bay Passage
trips.summary: A 2.5 hour sightseeing loop of Jervis Bay past sea cliffs, sea caves, Point Perpendicular Lighthouse and the shores of Hyams Beach, from mid-November to mid-May. The crew share local history along the way, and dolphins often join the cruise. It departs at 11am and 1:30pm, seven days a week.
highlights: Cliffs, sea caves and ancient rock formations
Past Point Perpendicular Lighthouse and Hyams Beach
Honeymoon Bay and other hidden coves
Dolphins often seen, and sometimes seals, sea eagles, turtles and seabirds

trips.title: South Coast Passage
trips.summary: A 2.5 hour trip by rigid inflatable boat along the remote sea cliffs of the Beecroft Peninsula, from November to May. The boat goes into sea caves, visits a seal colony, and bottlenose dolphins often swim at the bow. It departs at 8:30am daily and depends on wind and sea conditions.
highlights: Rigid inflatable small enough to go inside sea caves
Visit to a seal colony

trips.title: Stargazing Sea and Sky Cruise
trips.summary: A 3 hour evening cruise that leaves Huskisson at sunset, then watches the Milky Way rise with a guide from Jervis Bay Stargazing. The guide points out constellations and other features of the night sky before the boat returns to Huskisson wharf. It is listed for 7 November and depends on weather and cloud cover.

Runs all year round
